entry_conditions: Drawer closed or partly open with reliable caller-supplied zero-opening pose and fresh drawer_position; TCP high/free or plausibly near the front; observable gripper state; red supported in the drawer and blue outside. Reachability remains a high-level responsibility.
exit_conditions: Nominal exit is drawer_position safely above the unchanged strict 0.26-m threshold, drawer velocity near zero, front contact relinquished, and observable red/TCP co-motion after closure and initial lift. A closed gripper alone is not grasp proof.
overlap_role: All actions 0:470 are supervised. Actions 230:470 in every trajectory overlap red_transfer and include front release, retreat, red approach/descent, closure and initial lift: 240 actions per occurrence and 2,880 total.
successor_readiness: red_transfer can receive once drawer_position is above 0.26 and red is exposed because its supervision starts at 230. Nominal stronger readiness is closed fingers plus red/TCP upward co-motion near 470.
failure_signatures: Drawer remains at or below 0.26; drawer moves without matching TCP/front geometry; calibration jumps; fingers drag or miss the front; red/TCP XY misalignment; closure without red co-motion; red drop; IK nonconvergence or limit contact.
continuation_guidance: Continue through release and red pickup while observed relations follow a demonstrated phase. Switch early to red_transfer after opening/exposure or later after initial lift. Stop or replan rather than interpreting repeated nominal commands as demonstrated recovery.
limitations: Guidance is based on successful demonstrations at one cabinet calibration. It does not add success conditions, contact truth, recovery competence, collision checking or guarantees for large displaced/unreachable drawers.
